title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in China: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in China: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for China: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: Advance healthcare, guardianship, property, and notarial planning in mainland China relies on written instruments governed by the Civil Code, the Notarization Law, and local medical rules [1][3][7][13]. Organizing these records in advance prevents estate freeze delays and clarifies authority for appointed decision-makers [1][3][4].

steps.title: Palliative care coordination and advance medical directive limits
steps.html:
• Confirm available inpatient palliative, symptom-control, and hospice resources with treating hospitals under National Health Commission (NHC) of the PRC pilot care frameworks [6]. Care models vary by province and designated medical institution [6].
  • Clarify the regional legal boundary for living wills: mainland China does not yet enforce a single uniform national statute making living wills binding everywhere, whereas Article 78 of the Shenzhen Special Economic Zone Medical Regulations legally recognizes properly witnessed or notarized advance medical directives inside Shenzhen [7][13].
  • Outside Shenzhen, patients should document care preferences in writing, discuss them directly with attending clinicians and close family, and align medical decision-making with a formal guardian appointment where needed [1][6][7][13].

steps.title: Appointing a Voluntary Guardian (Yiding Jianhu) under the Civil Code
steps.html:
• Under Article 33 of the Civil Code of the PRC, an adult with full civil capacity may consult in advance with a close relative or another willing individual or organization and sign a written Voluntary Guardianship Agreement naming a guardian to manage personal care and property if civil capacity is later lost or limited [1].
  • Have Voluntary Guardianship agreements and personal-care/financial powers notarized through a local public notary under Articles 11 and 25 of the Notarization Law of the PRC [3], reviewed alongside Supreme People's Court of the PRC (Judicial & Notarial Reference) guidance [3][4]. For municipal examples covering bilingual or foreign-related notarial files, check Guangzhou Bureau of Justice - Foreign-Related Notary Public Services [8].
  • Ensure appointed guardians and trusted relatives hold clear written boundaries on medical consent, hospital billing access, and bank account management [1][3].

steps.title: Preparing a valid Will and protecting vulnerable dependents
steps.html:
• Draft or update a Will compliant with Book VI of the Civil Code of the PRC (Articles 1122, 1127, 1133-1147, and 1158), noting that under the Civil Code the latest legally valid will takes precedence rather than earlier notarized wills holding automatic priority [1].
  • Keep mandatory protective provisions in mind: Supreme People's Court typical heirship cases (18 December 2024) emphasize safeguarding statutory necessary shares for heirs who lack both labor capability and sources of livelihood, as well as honoring valid legacy-support agreements (yizeng fuyang xieyi) [1][4].
  • Where real property is located in a Chinese city, confirm inheritance notarization requirements with the notary office where the real estate sits (Notarization Law Art. 25), and verify residential hukou, marriage certificates, and property ownership certificates (Budongchan Quan Zheng) match exactly [1][3][8].

steps.title: Social insurance records, funeral rules, and Deed Tax Law readiness
steps.html:
• Gather the person's social security card, medical insurance reimbursement records, and personal basic pension account details governed by the Social Insurance Law of the PRC (Articles 14, 17, 38(8), and 49) so family members understand individual account inheritability and survivor benefits later [2].
  • Review real estate transfer planning with State Taxation Administration of the PRC rules in view: under Article 6(5) of the Deed Tax Law of the PRC, statutory heirs inheriting land or house ownership are exempt from deed tax, whereas transfers by will to non-statutory recipients may carry different tax treatment [5].
  • Note upcoming regulatory standards affecting medical documentation and funeral administration, including State Council Decree No. 824 (Revised Funeral and Interment Regulations, effective 30 March 2026) and the February 2026 circular establishing unified Medical Death Certificate coding (1 July 2026) and equal-validity electronic certificates (1 January 2027) [9][10].

steps.title: Cross-border Apostille preparation and bilingual family files
steps.html:
• Because mainland China joined the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention on 7 November 2023, Chinese notarized powers of attorney, kinship records, and civil documents destined for other Convention jurisdictions can be authenticated via Apostille by China's Competent Authorities rather than embassy legalization [11].
  • Foreign receiving institutions can check document authenticity via Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) - Consular Apostille Verification [12].
  • Assemble an indexed folder listing Chinese and overseas bank accounts, real property deeds, original identification cards, hukou records, wills, Voluntary Guardianship deeds, and translator requirements for family abroad [1][3][11].
